chunks: Rijal al-Kashshi: Hamduwayh, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from al-Fudhayl and Ibrahim, the two sons of Muhammad al-Ash'ari, who said:

When the news of the death of Bukayr ibn A'yan reached Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), he said: By Allah, Allah has placed him between the Messenger of Allah and the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon them).

key_terms.بَكِيرُ بْنُ أَعْيَنَ: Bukayr ibn A'yan, a companion of the Imams
key_terms.بَيْنَ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ وَأَمِيرِ الْمُؤْ: Between the Messenger of Allah and the Commander of the Faithful
key_terms.صَلَوَاتُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِمَا: Prayers of Allah be upon them both

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about Bukayr ibn A'yan's status after death?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Kashi highlights the high esteem in which Bukayr ibn A'yan was held by Imam al-Sadiq (AS), using the metaphor of being 'between' the Prophet and Imam Ali to signify a unique spiritual proximity or elevated rank in the afterlife. In Shia tradition, such expressions often denote a special status of closeness to the Ahl al-Bayt, reflecting Bukayr's role as a trusted companion and narrator. The statement underscores the Imam's authority to assess the spiritual standing of his contemporaries based on their fidelity and service.
